chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'Some of your freed slaves married into a family, and the women claimed that there was breastfeeding (radha') between them.' He said, 'As for one breastfeeding and two breastfeedings, it is of no consequence unless the nurse is a hired woman who resides with them.' He (peace be upon him) explicitly clarified in this narration that what is meant by that is what we have stated regarding one and two breastfeedings, excluding what exceeds that until it reaches the limit that causes prohibition, as we have clarified.
ai.seo_question: Does one or two breastfeedings cause marriage prohibition in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that isolated instances of breastfeeding (one or two times) do not establish the permanent prohibition of mahram relationships, unless the nurse is a hired resident who feeds the child consistently. This ruling distinguishes between casual nursing and the established legal threshold required for kinship ties, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the quality and duration of the act rather than mere occurrence.
